doc.title: James Hunter interviewed by Monk Rowe, Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018

title: Across the pond: Brexit, Trump and British politics
summary: The two compare interest in each other's politics, and Hunter gives views on Trump, May, Corbyn and the NHS.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: A British journalist I met reminded me of the phrase “across the pond.”
Which we probably both use to each other’s countries.

And we take a certain amount of interest in things across the pond like Brexit and so forth. And I wonder if it’s the same for you and your band mates. Do they observe what’s happening in the United States?

Certainly yeah. I mean with what’s going on here now, I mean there’s nobody that’s not aware of it. I mean you know American politics is usually at the forefront, and I suppose — of the British news, we’re all very aware of that, and maybe to a lesser extent the — America knows what’s going on with Britain. But it’s a sheer matter of scale really, because there’s a lot of America so there’s going to be a lot of people who aren’t aware of the Brexit thing. But very few people in England wouldn’t be aware of, you know, the current incumbent — how do I start to describe it — but yeah. Yeah everybody knows what’s going on, yeah.
Yeah. I suppose it’s starting to become explicable. You know it sounds fanciful but you know it’s hard to believe he got voted in, isn’t it?

Yeah I mean but we’ve got — our leader at home is this vacuous follower who basically will do anything to latch on to power including falling in with, you know, sort of extreme right wing parties like the DUP you know. That’s how she got her false majority to stay in power after a hung Parliament. I mean she called a what do you call it, she called a general election thinking she was going to get a huge mandate and she made a cut of it. Yeah, ah well, I’m a Corbyn man you know. I want him in. Because people say all the other stuff about him and a lot of it — I mean we’re dominated by a right wing press at home. Most of it is owned by one Australian. And anyone who doesn’t want the National Health Service to be sold off to various bids is regarded as a hard line Marxist. It’s ridiculous. The National Health Service was founded after the last war and it was state- run healthcare for anybody, whether they can afford it or not. And the — our government sees that as an asset to be demolished and sold off. They’ve always seen it like that. Ever since 1945 they’ve been trying to destroy it.
Well some things are sort of the same across the pond. Who are your musical heroes?
